U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer Speaks at Security Forum
# viktor orban· us trade policy· usmca· aspen security forum· biden administration· china relations· jamieson greer· john phelan· manufacturing sector· national security· nick scottwine· pentagon· section 232· section 301· steve clemens· tariff strategy· trump administration

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer argues that adversaries exploit low-cost autonomous systems against high-cost defenses, necessitating robust air strategies while Hungary receives EU aid despite Viktor Orban's opposition. He outlines three trade metrics: reducing deficits, raising wages eroded by Iran-driven inflation, and boosting manufacturing's GDP share from 9.5% to match OECD averages. Greer details reciprocal agreements with nine nations for supply chain security, notes USMCA renegotiations to block Chinese goods via Mexico, and confirms bipartisan support for tariffs on EVs and solar panels. Ultimately, the discussion asserts that divorcing economics from geopolitical realities is impossible, requiring a cohesive policy balancing national security with market stability. That all makes a ton of sense, but I would argue that the sectors you just mentioned, whether broadly defined or narrowly defined, are still within the national security realm.

I understand.

If you look at where we were before the Supreme Court case came down striking down the IEPA tariffs, we were pretty much kind of there, right?

Just one by one, we're going through, we're identifying all these unfair trading practices to get at the underlying unfairness and imbalance and lack of reciprocity in the trading system.
So we're going to conclude these investigations.
We may start some more.
